scope: Code review of the integrated native generation pipeline and three offline reproductions using repository fixtures; no paid model calls or manual user-game changes by the review.

reproductions.method: Generate a fixture draft with a browser callback returning unverified/infrastructure; save its checkpoint; resume the same request with a healthy callback and a submit operation.
reproductions.observed: Continuation returns the previous unavailable-browser failure; healthy callback is never invoked.

reproductions.method: Pass two reports to repair_route with the same mechanics check name/message and different failed case IDs inside evidence; pass the first fingerprint to the second call.
reproductions.observed: Both fingerprints match; strategy changes from structural to regenerate despite different failed mechanics.

reproductions.method: Keep fixture case IDs, actions, keyboard keys and continuous flags; replace desktop/touch movement assertions with a literal score greater than -1; call validate_mechanics and preserve_mechanics.
reproductions.observed: Both validations accept the weakened assertions. This demonstrates an acceptance-contract gap, not an observed model exploit or a passing live game.

limitations: The 33 skipped Python checks are not passes.
No fresh end-to-end paid generation, rendered art assessment or isolated browser run was launched for this review.
The observed active user generation was read only and is not a controlled comparison.
Existing PostgreSQL and browser evidence belongs to earlier verification and is not counted as a new run here.
Contest WebView host and device remain unspecified.
